Release: survival probabilities

release_model.Rd

The external model gives survival probabilities, not only a ranking of subjects: either a Cox model's coefficients together with its baseline cumulative hazard, or the model's interval hazards for each of your subjects directly. Give either

  • beta and baseline: the external hazard of a subject with covariates \(z\) in interval \(k\) is \(\tilde h_k(z) = 1 - \exp\{-\exp(z^\top\tilde\beta)\, \Delta\Lambda_0(k)\}\); or

  • hazard: the external interval hazards \(\tilde h_{ik}\) themselves.

Survival probabilities are what a discrete-time target needs for the Kullback-Leibler divergence, which compares the two models' hazards in every interval. With beta, the release also supports everything release_coef() supports.

Usage

release_model(beta = NULL, baseline = NULL, hazard = NULL, Q = NULL)

Arguments

beta

Named external coefficients, as in release_coef().

baseline

The external baseline cumulative-hazard increments over your intervals \(1, \dots, K\): \(\Delta\Lambda_0(k) = \Lambda_0(t_k) - \Lambda_0(t_{k-1})\), with \(t_k\) the end of interval \(k\). Non-negative, one value per interval of the target.

hazard

Instead of beta and baseline: an \(n \times K\) matrix whose row \(i\), column \(k\) is the external probability that subject \(i\) of your data has the event in interval \(k\) given that it reached the interval. Rows in the order of your data.

Q

Optional precision matrix of beta, as in release_coef(), for the Mahalanobis divergence.

Value

An object of class "bregsurv_release", a list with form = "model", beta, baseline, hazard and Q (those not given are NULL).

See also

cv.bregsurv(); the other releases, release_records(), release_coef(), release_score(); the targets, target_cox(), target_ncc() and target_discrete().

Examples

data(ExampleData_discrete)
release_model(beta = ExampleData_discrete$beta_external,
              baseline = ExampleData_discrete$baseline_external)
#> Release: survival probabilities, 5 coefficients with a baseline hazard over 6 intervals
